messages:
maya: heads up — nightly eval (summarization-edgecases) shows a sharp quality drop for rw-llama3-70b quant profile run (INT8/FP8 variants). accuracy down 92.1% -> 85.7% on the prompt set, lots of weird trailing token "ghost" artifacts. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/1900123456 :eyes:
ryan: ugh. did this start after last night's model push or a config change? any suspect commits?
maya: looks tied to PR #452 (quant-profile tweaks + new per-layer clip). commit: a1b2c3d4. The hosted FP8 baseline is fine; the INT8-calib job shows the failures.
sam: can you paste an example bad output vs expected? even one prompt is enough.
maya: sure — using prompt id summarization-edgecases/0234
```
PROMPT: "Summarize the webpage about the council meeting in one paragraph."
EXPECTED: "At the meeting, council members discussed budget reallocations and approved the new park plan, emphasizing community engagement and a phased timeline."
INT8-FAIL: "At the meeting, council members discussed budget reallocations and approved the new park plan, emphasizing community engagement and a phased timeline. \u2581ghost\u2581ghost\u2581ghost"
FP8-BL: "At the meeting, council members discussed budget reallocations and approved the new park plan, emphasizing community engagement and a phased timeline."
```
ryan: that trailing repeating token (ghost) smells like a rounding/overflow in quant scales or a KV cache misindex. do we see this across many samples?
maya: yes ~18% of the failed prompts have the ghost suffix or short hallucinations. it's not just repetition, sometimes extra unrelated sentence.
tess: I ran a quick local reproducer against the same model+quant profile (a1b2c3d4) — when I force `--no-kv-cache` the ghost token disappears but latency increases. so kv-path might interact badly with quant scales. logs attached: `layer17_scale=3.4e+01 overflow_count=12` and a couple of `quant_clip_exceeded` warnings.
sam: interesting — layer17_scale is suspiciously high. which kernel selection did runtime pick?
tess: runtime log: `selected_kernel: matmul_opt_v2_fused_fp8` for FP8 run; for INT8 it chose `int8_pack_gemm` and then `fallback_matmul` on some seq lengths.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: nightly-run/1900123456 completed for experiment: quant-profile-v5 (status: failure, checks: 47/52)
ryan: ok next steps: 1) bisect quant-profile diff around PR#452 2) reproduce minimal repro (single prompt, short seq) with flags: `--quant-mode int8 --calib-table v5` 3) try `--force-calib-seed 42` and `--no-kv-cache` to isolate kv interaction.
maya: starting bisect now, will run 4 checkpoints (v3->v4->v5) and post results. running local script: 
```
./tools/nightly_eval.sh --model rw-llama3-70b --profile v5 --promptset summarization-edgecases --seed 2026 --limit 200
```
will also test `--profile v4` to confirm regression boundary.
sam: if layer17 scale is big, maybe the per-layer clip introduced too-aggressive max abs leading to asymmetric quantization issues. can you dump the per-layer clip tables? maya: dumping now (snippet):
```
layer17_clip: 1.2e-02  (v4)
layer17_clip: 1.1e-03  (v5)
```
ryan: whoa, v5 clip for layer17 is an order of magnitude smaller — that could push the dynamic range into more quantization noise and cause strange tokens when combined with cached KV.
tess: i just ran `--profile v5 --no-kv-cache --quant-mode int8` locally: accuracy jumps back to 90.8% (still below FP8 baseline but much better). confirms kv+tight-clip = failure mode.
maya: bisect results quick summary: v3 ok, v4 ok, v5 fails. regression introduced in PR#452. full bisect log: https://ci.internal/redwood/bisect/1900123456
sam: given that, immediate mitigation = rollback v5 clip for layer17 (or widen clip bounds) and re-run nightly. we should also add a targeted fuzz test combining KV cache + tight clip values.
ryan: agree. also add eval gating: any per-layer clip change that changes max_abs by >3x should fail automatic promote until manual review.
maya: opened rollback PR #457 to revert per-layer clip change for layer17 and a follow-up PR #458 to add fuzz test and gating rule.
ryan: can you run a quick smoke after rollback locally and then trigger a new nightly?
maya: running smoke now: `./tools/smoke_eval.sh --model rw-llama3-70b --profile v5-rollback --limit 50` — preliminary: accuracy 92.0%, ghost token rate <1%.
tess: nice. i'll own the follow-up eval ticket to add KV+clip fuzzing and a couple unit tests for per-layer quant scale sanity. assigning to @sam.
sam: got it — will add tests and iterate on calibration algorithm to avoid extreme clamp reductions.
ryan: pls also add a short postmortem blurb in #postmortems and tag infra for a follow-up on kernel selection heuristics (some kernels fallbacked unexpectedly).
maya: noted. i'll post a short incident note and link PRs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam: quick todo list in thread: [rollback PR merged], [new nightly run triggered], [fuzz tests + gating] — i'll update when tests land.
maya: closing the loop: rollback merged, nightly scheduled (run id 1900123578). will update thread after final results.
